heading: Networks can fit corrupted labels while test performance degrades
definition: as the fraction of randomly corrupted labels rises from none to all, networks still fit the training set perfectly while test error rises steadily toward chance, so they capture the remaining signal while memorizing the noise.
summary: Independent image-classification studies reproduce perfect training fit alongside worsening test performance as label corruption increases. This does not hold in every setting: some training regimes prevent perfect fitting, and intermediate amounts of uniformly random label noise can leave test performance nearly unchanged.

suggested_status.by_scale: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size contain '<1B' and 'not stated'. At <1B, fitting and degradation components have independent support, but the complete literal V4 remains unresolved. In size-unspecified image models, the sampled joint pattern reaches R2, while unrestricted V4 is contested. No complete-trajectory status is established at 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B; toy settings are not separately bucketed.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to V4 as written, while its restricted empirical pattern reaches R2. Independent WideResNet-18 experiments jointly establish perfect training fit and monotonic test-accuracy decline across an endpoint-inclusive corruption sweep (arXiv:1904.12286#R1,#R2,#R4,#R6,#R8,#R10,#R12). Binary-image CNN/FC experiments independently report zero training error with increasing generalization error (arXiv:1805.08522#R1,#R2,#R3,#R4,#R5,#R6). However, VGG-11 fails to fit fully corrupted CIFAR-10 under multi-step learning-rate decay (arXiv:2112.08798#R4), and an MNIST CNN reports little intermediate uniform-noise sensitivity (arXiv:2202.03674#R1). These contest unconditional perfect fitting and steady degradation. counts: versions.V4.verdicts records support, limits_scope and challenges; those categories do not establish replication of every clause.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched corruption sweeps with clean-test evaluation, sufficiently converged training, and fixed architecture and optimization would determine whether the reported failures persist under comparable protocols. Denser sampling would test smoothness; separate clean/noisy-subset measurements would test the proposed signal-versus-memorization explanation. Complete trajectories in explicitly sized billion-parameter models would change the scale assessment.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: Zhang et al. trained Inception, Alexnet, and MLP 1x512 on CIFAR10 with increasing random label corruption.
original_result.result: Zhang et al. plotted test error after convergence for corruption fractions from 0 to 1. These results give no numerical error values or corresponding training-fit measurements, so they do not establish both perfect fitting and worsening test performance.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Smoothness between sampled corruption levels across the complete range under a fixed architecture, corruption mechanism, training recipe and evaluation endpoint.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines for arXiv:2006.02909, arXiv:2308.01609 and arXiv:2103.13872 explicitly distinguish sampled trends from behavior between rates. arXiv:1904.12286 supplies a joint endpoint-inclusive sampled sweep, so absence of any such sweep is not a global gap. counts: versions.V4.rows_by_evidence_form describes extracted evidence forms and does not establish continuous behavior.

untested.what: A causal decomposition of the complete corruption-response curve into retained signal learning and noise memorization.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines for arXiv:1904.12286, arXiv:2002.09956 and arXiv:2202.10788 distinguish aggregate fitting/degradation from separately measured mechanisms. arXiv:2009.00329#R5 supplies partial-noise coexistence evidence, without this full-range decomposition. counts: versions.V4.main_rows_by_operation does not encode whether the proposed causal separation was established.

untested.what: The complete V4 trajectory in billion-parameter generative language models, including models above 100B parameters.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size contain only '<1B' and 'not stated'; these keyword-derived fields are incomplete coverage indicators. V4_6 nevertheless reports an unextracted Qwen2.5-7B partial-noise fitting result in arXiv:2610.04507, so larger-model testing is not wholly absent. That record's untested-parts line excludes the full corruption trajectory; the synthetic-transformer records likewise do not supply it.

wording_issues.issue: Literal perfection exceeds several reported endpoints. AllConv converges with incomplete training fit; the SGD-generalization record supplies a shared below-0.2% stopping threshold; mixup-paper ERM has nonzero subset errors; language-pretrained GPT-2 has near-complete rather than perfect fitting in the cited conditions.

wording_issues.phrase: networks still fit the training set perfectly
wording_issues.issue: Fitting depends on architecture, input distribution and optimization horizon. Fashion-MNIST CNN training accuracy declines under corruption; VGG-11 fails at complete corruption with multi-step learning-rate decay. Low-variance toy-MNIST models retain high training error despite SGD targeting zero error. For the default 5-layer GIN with 300 hidden units on PPA, noise memorization is absent in the 37-class condition, explicitly including the 30% subset with 20% corruption. Reduced 6- and 2-class conditions show partial noisy-label fitting; the 2-class condition is slightly more robust. Across 5%, 30% and 100% PPA subsets, smaller subsets show stronger noise fitting, while full or large subsets are described as robust.

The fitting clause also needs the objective and measurement scope. Supervised contrastive training does not reach exact zero training error within the cited high-noise budget; unreported residual error prevents assessing near-zero fitting. Regularized modular-addition models can avoid corrupted-label memorization. FedAvg client fitting does not establish global fitting. The frozen-feature PathMNIST classical head on a 10,000-image subset at 50% symmetric noise after 60 epochs has 7.4% agreement with flipped targets and 92.5% agreement on uncorrupted examples. Table 4 supplies nominal chance agreement of 11.1%, but no conditional null specifically for the flipped subset.

The records include a reversed direction for Xavier-initialized CIFAR-100 ResNet-18. An MNIST CNN shows negligible sensitivity in a β sweep from 0.2 to 0.9, with uniform-noise correct-label probability α matched to generated-noise correct-label rate η; rounded plotted limits are not exact correct-label probabilities. Underparameterized MNIST FCNNs show the opposite test-error direction, while underparameterized CIFAR-10 CNNs show no significant effect; both contradict steady increase, with perfect training fit untested. Synthetic ReLU experiments report zero training classification error, including p=0.5. Their lower-dimensional tempered profiles show clean test error linear in p, whereas higher-dimensional profiles show benign behavior at lower noise and appreciable clean error near p=0.5. Here clean test error uses the constant +1 target, and p is the probability of a negative label.

wording_issues.phrase: test error rises steadily toward chance
wording_issues.issue: Degradation need not be gradual throughout the range. LeNet-5 reaches chance at modest MNIST corruption, without condition-specific training-fit attainment being reported; the CIFAR-Easy CNN collapses before complete randomization. Speech encoders show a plateau followed by a sharp high-noise collapse. For the wav2vec2.0 large best-validation sweep at 100% training scale, the matched 0%-replacement test accuracy is 94.7%, and the adjacent 70%-replacement condition gives 85.4%. Uniform-noise resistance in the noise-concentration study persists until high corruption.

Held-out metrics are not interchangeable. The segmentation records report Dice or IoU and include essentially unchanged performance under their randomized-label conditions. Cityscapes random-flipping probabilities 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 give 64.7%, 64.6% and 64.7% mIoU against a cited Chen et al. (2017) clean-label baseline of 64.8% mIoU; that baseline is not a clean-label rerun. Other records report relation-extraction F1 or sleep-apnea kappa rather than classification test error.

wording_issues.phrase: the fraction of randomly corrupted labels
wording_issues.issue: A common corruption axis requires a sampling definition. Incorrect-class replacement can retain class information at its maximum rate; fixed-alternative flips can lead to alternative-label learning. Structured code-output corruption and segmentation retention/flipping procedures also differ from dataset-wide independent random relabeling.

Partial-corruption series cannot independently establish the complete trajectory. The joint-optimization, PAC-Bayes ReLU, regularizer-mirror-descent and text-classification records stop short of complete randomization. Training-only and test-only results from different experiments cannot be combined into a matched full-range measurement.

The endpoint needs an appropriate metric and corruption definition. Complete incorrect-class corruption in the MNIST MLP gives below-chance accuracy; fully randomized CIFAR-10 pretrained GPT-2 also reports below-nominal-chance accuracy with an unresolved endpoint interpretation. Zero TACRED F1 is not an established chance baseline, and the taxonomy record leaves numerical chance endpoints unresolved.

wording_issues.phrase: so they capture the remaining signal while memorizing the noise
wording_issues.issue: Aggregate training fit and test degradation do not separately identify the proposed mechanism. Deep pNML reports those aggregate measurements; the AND-mask comparator supplies more direct coexistence evidence at partial noise. Corrupting test labels, as in the input-randomness study, prevents an independent assessment of retained clean-label prediction.

method_sensitivity.factor: Optimizer, learning rate, duration and checkpoint selection
method_sensitivity.what: High learning rates leave noisy-label fitting incomplete in PreAct ResNet-32; lowering the rate permits near-zero loss. MNIST MLP constant-rate Adam at 200 epochs gives final training-accuracy fractions 1.000→0.962 from ρ=0→1. SGD interpolates at ρ=0,0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1; selected cosine-Adam conditions reach 99.9% training accuracy. Extended constant-rate Adam remains short of interpolation at high noise; M measures changed-label memorization, not overall accuracy. CIFAR-10 PreAct ResNet CE best test accuracies at corruption fractions 0.2,0.4,0.6 are 88.1%,84.3%,77.7%, versus final-ten-epoch averages 81.7%,65.0%,44.9%. Speech-model selected-checkpoint accuracy can exceed final-checkpoint accuracy, and high-noise curves contain sharp transitions. At 100% training scale, the matched clean best-validation test accuracy is 94.7%; the 70%-replacement condition gives 85.4%.

At 75% MNIST randomization, small high-aIQ LeNet-300-100 retains 84.68% accuracy versus 36.99% for the large variant; both approach chance at complete randomization. ConvNet width determines whether 20%-corrupted CIFAR-10 labels are interpolated. Underparameterized MNIST FCNNs show reduced test error with label noise; CIFAR-10 CNNs show no significant test-error effect. These challenge V4's predicted increase; perfect training fit remains untested. Double-descent peaks increase. PPA experiments use a default 5-layer GIN with 300 hidden units: at 20% noise, memorization is absent with 37 classes and fitting is partial with 6 or 2 classes; 2 classes are described as slightly more robust than 6. Fitting also depends on graph order and sample size. Smaller subsets fit noise more strongly; the 30% 37-class subset lacks memorization, and full or large subsets are described as robust.

method_sensitivity.factor: Loss, sample weighting and target selection
method_sensitivity.what: SuperLoss and DiscrimLoss reduce CIFAR-100 WideResNet training fit relative to cross-entropy. CIFAR10 ResNet-18 CE and CE-fix interpolate where supervised contrastive training fails to reach exact zero training error within its high-corruption budget; the residual error is unreported, so near-zero fitting cannot be determined. RLL and normalized MSE leave incomplete fitting in the reported image-classification conditions. MNIST MAE preserves high test accuracy from random initialization but produces CCE-like overfitting after CCE pretraining; this last comparison is verdict-based without extracted rows.

Strong dropout and mixup suppress corrupted-label fitting relative to ordinary CIFAR-10 ERM; selected settings sometimes change with noise rate. Modular-addition weight decay changes simultaneous fitting/generalization into partial memorization, absent memorization or chance performance; dropout can prevent complete fitting. Its coexistence condition establishes perfect fit, not a steady test-error trajectory. Digits-MLP noisy-validation early stopping gives 3.3% and 5.3% corrupted-label memorization at 10% and 60% noise; strong weight decay gives 4.3% and 32.3%, versus matched minimally regularized MLP values of 100%. These are means over five seeds. ResNet-110 authors attribute incomplete high-noise fitting to augmentation without a matched extracted ablation. Its ε=1 endpoint has training-accuracy fraction 0.36 under incorrect-class replacement, not label-independent uniform randomization.

method_sensitivity.factor: Corruption distribution and meaning of its maximum rate
method_sensitivity.what: Complete incorrect-class MNIST corruption gives 0.5% test accuracy, whereas SU and PERM give 10.1%. Fixed-alternative flipping can learn alternative labels after its transition. A MNIST CNN shows little sensitivity to intermediate uniform noise but a sharp drop under neighboring-class biased noise around correct-label probability 0.5. The sweep is β=0.2–0.9 in increments of 0.1; correct-label probability α is matched to generated-noise rate η, not equated with β or rounded plot limits. Cityscapes-3 uses specified noise transition matrices: rank-3 matrices retain class distinctions and near-clean performance; rank-2 matrices erase the distinction between classes 1/2, 1/3 or 2/3 and sharply reduce IoU. Rank-1 matrices have identical columns and zero pairwise class-distribution distances; their reported outcome is overfitting, not numerical IoU.

method_sensitivity.factor: Pretraining, encoder freezing and adapter rank
method_sensitivity.what: Language-pretrained vision-adapted GPT-2 fits corrupted labels substantially better than scratch GPT-2; complete-corruption fit also differs between CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Frozen SimCLR and MoCo ResNet34 encoders retain high CIFAR10 accuracy over the reported symmetric-noise sweep, with encoder-freezing preference depending on noise level. AG News and DeiT-Tiny higher-rank LoRA adapters approach or attain complete fitting where lower-rank adapters remain incomplete under their fixed training budgets. The AG News clean-label baseline exceeds 99% training accuracy at all ranks, including 32 and 64; those higher ranks approach 100% training accuracy at 40% symmetric noise. These adapter comparisons establish fitting components rather than a complete test-error trajectory.

method_sensitivity.factor: Input geometry, variance and signal scaling
method_sensitivity.what: Synthetic ReLU experiments report zero training classification error, including p=0.5. Increasing dimension relative to sample size changes approximately linear noise-dependent clean-error profiles into near-zero clean error at lower positive noise, with appreciable clean error near p=0.5. Figure 1 compares dimensions 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000; numerical curve values are unstated. Low-variance toy-MNIST models retain high training error despite SGD targeting zero error; increasing variance permits memorization and zero training error. Hinge-loss ReLU results have benign-interpolation, harmful-interpolation and non-overfitting regimes under theorem-specific margin and signal-strength assumptions. Leaky-ReLU KKT guarantees require the specified covariance, cluster and signal-scaling assumptions; they do not supply an unconditional clean-error curve.

Adversarial training preserves a correct/incorrect-label fitting gap and reduces corruption damage relative to standard training. Perfect training fit is undetermined for the standard-training rows and incomplete for the adversarial-training rows; their temporal learning-order evidence concerns V6 separately. PGD-AT fails to converge at 80% noise. TRADES reports an increasing generalization gap, which alone establishes neither perfect training fit nor steadily worsening test error and supplies no V4 support. Algorithm and perturbation budget matter. OrthoGrad reduces small-data MNIST CNN fitting relative to Adam, while both methods eventually memorize corrupted CIFAR-10 labels in the ResNet-18 extension. Increasing gradient-agreement requirements in AND-mask prevents memorization that its standard baseline exhibits.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task, model family and federated measurement location
method_sensitivity.what: FedAvg server and client noisy-label memorization differ; its i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. comparisons also change noise parameters, preventing isolation of heterogeneity alone. Code2Seq fits corrupted outputs incompletely, VarMisuse localization models fail under high structured corruption, and CodeBERT training is impaired under complete docstring corruption. Sparse-parity Transformers achieve perfect clean generalization while training accuracy converges at 1−η without fitting flipped targets; this is partial V4 evidence. Some runs overfit noise only after many additional post-convergence iterations, a separate V6 temporal result. LSTMs fail to generalize even in the clean comparison. FDA transformer memorization depends on model configuration and uses first-answer-token accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation targets, metric definition and run selection
method_sensitivity.what: Corrupting both training and test labels changes the meaning of generalization degradation. Self-Adaptive Training's noisy-training/noisy-validation accuracy gap is not clean-test error. Binarized-MNIST FCN results describe retained runs trained to perfect accuracy without convergence success rates. The CNN feature-learning lower bound evaluates a distribution containing reused training noise patches, so its test error is not directly interchangeable with ordinary clean-target error.
